Use case: compositing.
Image 1 is the edit target: one close-up overhead game-ground patch, 1670 × 1090. Fill its white missing area as a seamless continuation of the supplied top and right neighbour strips. Image 2 is a supporting ground-material reference: match the fine scale and low grass, but keep the new earth quieter with fewer outlined grains.
Preserve the topmost 15% and rightmost 10% exactly in place. Across the rest of the upper band, let warm brown soil and muted olive grass extend upward in irregular natural fingers, so there is no straight horizontal colour boundary. Preserve the old orange leaves only in the narrow existing contact; add no new leaves to the new ground. Warm brown near camp gradually becomes neutral medium umber farther down.
New ground: broad quiet areas of flat matte compacted earth, subtle fine mineral grain, tiny sparse angular grit, irregular patches of low short olive grass. Paint continuous soil surfaces with shallow scuffs and tonal variation, not a field of separate outlined objects. Crisp fine hand-painted 2D game texture, at character scale, soft even daylight, exact overhead angle. Natural small detail with no blur or sharpening halo.
This right-hand patch stays entirely road-free. No roads, paths, paving, standing foliage, trees, bushes, flowers, large stones, props, water, buildings, characters, labels, grid, frame, black border or vignette. No honeycomb, ring patterns, bubbles, pits, scales, bead-like grains or embossed surfaces. Do not repeat identical grass clumps. Fill to the left and bottom edges. One finished continuous ground patch, no divided panels or overview.

Use case: compositing. Image 1 is the edit target, a single close-up top-down game-ground patch, 1670 × 1090. Fill the white missing area. Preserve the topmost 15% and rightmost 8% exactly in place, matching the scale, colours, lighting and fine painted ground of the right neighbour.
Continue the ONE existing stone camp path visible near the upper right, entering the white area around x=1320. Let it bend gently LEFT as it proceeds downwards, staying away from the right contact, and cross the bottom near x=1000. In the first third keep a short continuation of the same worn stones, then let the paving break up gradually into a NARROW compacted dirt footpath, about 65–90 pixels across. The dirt trail should remain clearly readable but softly worn, without kerbs. Do not add junctions, side roads, loops, or paving elsewhere.
All other new ground is quiet matte brown earth and broad irregular patches of short subdued olive grass. Keep subtle fine mineral grain with sparse tiny angular grit, continuous soil surfaces and low-contrast blade strokes. Avoid bumpy or deeply outlined grains. Warm ground near the upper camp contact gradually becomes neutral brown toward the bottom, through organic shapes without a straight line. The old orange leaves belong only to the narrow existing top border; no new red or orange leaves in the generated area.
Crisp hand-painted 2D terrain at character scale, exact overhead view, no perspective or horizon, soft even daylight. No buildings, objects, standing rocks, trees, bushes, flowers, water, characters, text, grid, borders, black fade or vignette. No honeycomb, rings, bubbles, patterned soil, bead-like pebbles, large repeated green rosettes, blur or sharpened halos. Fill to left and bottom. One continuous finished ground patch.

Use case: compositing. Fill the white missing area of this single close-up overhead game terrain patch, 1670 × 1088. Preserve the topmost 12% and rightmost 10% exactly in place. Seamlessly continue the supplied fine brown earth and low olive grass into the new area at the same scale, lighting and colour family.
Keep this entire patch road-free. Mix broad quiet patches of matte compacted brown earth with irregular areas of fine short muted olive grass, tending slightly toward cooler, darker umber in a few natural shallow patches. Soil is a continuous surface with subtle mineral grain, tiny scattered angular grit and light wear. It should not look like thousands of outlined grains. Let some dirt patches remain quite plain. Grass is low and fine, with small varied blade strokes and soft irregular edges. No repeating clumps or oversized rosette plants. Keep fine detail crisp, with no blur or sharpening halo.
No roads, paths, paving, leaves, flowers, trees, bushes, standing rocks, props, water, structures, characters, text, grid, border or vignette. No honeycomb, rings, crater holes, bubbles, beads, scales or embossed texture. No straight colour divisions. Extend every existing patch naturally across the supplied contact, leaving broad open space for separate game foliage later. Fill to the left and bottom canvas edges. Exact overhead game-art view, one continuous finished ground texture, not an overview or collage.

Use case: compositing. Fill the white missing area in this single close-up overhead game-ground patch, 1670 × 1088. Preserve the topmost 12% and rightmost 8% exactly. Continue the supplied brown earth and low olive grass naturally with the same scale, colours, painted finish and soft daylight.
Continue ONLY the faint narrow dirt footpath already entering from the top near x=760. Let it drift gently down-left toward x=650 near the bottom; allow its edges to become softer and slightly narrower, still a readable 60–80 pixel foot trail. No new paving or stone roads. No additional trails, branches, rings, tracks, crossings or loops.
Elsewhere leave broad quiet open ground: flat matte brown earth with fine subtle mineral grain and very sparse tiny grit, mixed with irregular shallow patches of short muted olive grass. Towards the lower-left add a little cooler darker brown soil and some plain bare dirt patches. Ground remains continuous, crisp and natural at character scale. Avoid dense outlined grains or repeated decorative clumps. Match the top and right through irregular organic shapes, without straight colour borders or a blurred joining band.
No red leaves or other fallen leaf decoration. No trees, bushes, flowers, large rosette plants, standing rocks, props, buildings, water, characters, text, grid, frames, black edges or vignette. No honeycomb, circles, holes, bubbles, embossed texture, blur or sharpening halos. Fill to left and bottom edges. Exact overhead view, one finished terrain patch, not a panorama or collage.
